claims.summary: Smolensky's MOD3 lower bound implies a degree/descent scope gap: H_n=product_i(1+(zeta-1)x_i)+product_i(1+(zeta²-1)x_i), zeta²+zeta+1=0 over F4, is binary multilinear of degree<=n with O(n)-size depth<=4 unbounded-fan-in arithmetic circuits over F4, but has no polynomial-size fixed-depth F2 arithmetic circuits even agreeing on Boolean inputs. Its Boolean field relation has a degree-2n certificate. For n>=2, the satisfiable complete-map source {y-H_n,y²-y}, W=1,T=B=n,D=n² fits weighted degree descent but does not permit a fixed-depth polynomial-size binary map.
claims.assessment: Attributed scope corollary of Smolensky 1987 Theorem 2 and his root-of-unity construction. Degree/membership/rank descent remains valid. No new circuit lower-bound technique, hard CNF, general IPS certificate lower bound, or Frege lower bound is claimed.
claims.rationale: Separates the degree-only source route from an unsupported constant-depth extension-field transfer for the IPS alternative. Classical consequence, no independent novelty claimed.
claims.next_action: Keep the binary circuit field explicit in IPS work; construct actual legal source maps on the degree route without assuming depth preservation.

relationships: Clarifies a circuit-complexity property not promised by the degree, membership and rank theorem; does not correct or obstruct its stated conclusion.
The existing transfer uses F2 input and proof circuits; compact F4 representations cannot silently replace that circuit model.
